priceNote: Q2 2026 blowout — revenue $1.94B (+93% YoY) vs $1.81B est., EPS $0.41 vs $0.35 est., US commercial +149% YoY — sent shares +15% after-hours from the $125.65 close as FY26 guide was raised to $8.15–8.16B (from $7.65–7.66B). Watch premarket follow-through into the Aug 4 regular session.
summary: Palantir just posted its strongest quarter yet — 93% YoY revenue growth, a 155% Rule-of-40 score, and a ~$500M FY guidance raise — breaking the prior 3-quarter sell-the-news pattern with a +15% after-hours pop. But that pop compresses upside to the $182 Street consensus to roughly +26%, under our 30% conviction bar, while the stock still trades near 70x forward earnings. Fundamentals are excellent; the entry price is no longer cheap.

risks: Post-pop chase risk — the +15% after-hours move can fade fast if the Aug 4 regular session doesn't hold the gap; 1 of the last 4 quarters (Q1 2026, May) still fell -6.93% despite a beat
Upside to consensus has compressed to ~26% (below the 30% conviction gate) — no longer a fresh-entry 'cheap' setup even with blowout fundamentals
Still-rich valuation — ~70x forward earnings even after the growth re-acceleration; any deceleration triggers violent multiple compression
UK/EU regulatory friction — Metropolitan Police contract was blocked in mid-2026 and NHS remains under scrutiny, even as the UK MOD relationship (£750M contract) deepens elsewhere
Hyperscaler competition — Azure AI, AWS Bedrock, Databricks all building competing enterprise AI tooling
Government budget/appropriations risk — US public sector still a large share of revenue; DOGE reviews and CR uncertainty can delay task orders despite the NGC2 win
Hawkish Fed dot plot (only 1 cut projected in 2026) keeps discount rates elevated for long-duration, high-multiple software names

estimateDates.note: Beat: $1.94B rev (+93% YoY) vs $1.81B est.; EPS $0.41 vs $0.35 est.; US commercial +149% YoY
Raised from prior $7.65–7.66B guide; US commercial now guided >$3.42B, up from prior >$3.22B
Watch whether guide-raise momentum holds and US commercial growth stays >100% YoY

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed has held 3.50–3.75% through mid-2026; the latest FOMC dot plot shows just one cut in 2026 (to ~3.44%) and one more in 2027 — a more hawkish path than markets had hoped, keeping pressure on long-duration, high-multiple software names.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core inflation still running above target. Government contracts (a large share of PLTR revenue) are largely inflation-insulated, but continued Fed hawkishness raises the effective discount rate applied to PLTR's 70x+ forward earnings.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: AI-software valuations are broadly under scrutiny for being stretched relative to an elevated cost of capital. PLTR's blowout Q2 print bucks that narrative on hard fundamentals, but the whole group remains rate-sensitive to any further hawkish repricing.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — a hawkish Fed dot plot (only one cut projected in 2026) pressures high-multiple AI software broadly. PLTR's Q2 beat-and-raise provides a fundamental offset, but doesn't eliminate multiple-compression risk if rate expectations shift further hawkish.

entryStrategy.verdict: PLTR just delivered its best quarter yet (93% rev growth, guide raised ~$500M) and popped +15% after-hours — but upside to the $182 consensus has compressed to ~26%, under our conviction bar. HOLD at $144: let the post-earnings dust settle and add on a pullback toward $125–130 rather than chasing the gap.

catalystSpot.preRunup: PLTR typically drifts flat-to-slightly-up into earnings on elevated expectations rather than building a large pre-print run; the actual print — not positioning — drives the move. Q2 2026 saw only a modest pre-announcement pop before the real +15% move came after the beat itself.

postWin.note: 3 of the last 4 quarters produced day-of/after-hours gains (Q2 2025 +7.85%, Q4 2025 +6.85%, Q2 2026 +15%), breaking the earlier 'sell-the-news' pattern. Q2 2026 (Aug 3, 2026) was the strongest: 93% YoY revenue growth + a ~$500M FY guide raise.

postLose.note: Q1 2026 (May 4, 2026) beat on revenue but shares still fell -6.93% as the guidance raise was seen as too modest relative to sky-high expectations — the lone miss-reaction in an otherwise strong run.

spotSizing.reason: Even after the Q2 blowout, upside to the $182 Street consensus has compressed to ~26% — below the 30% margin-of-safety bar — while the stock still trades near 70x forward earnings. Execution quality (93% rev growth, Rule of 40 = 155%) supports holding, not chasing an aggressive new entry at post-pop prices. Keep to 3–4% of portfolio.
